questions.question: Discuss the advantages, limitations, and precautions of the Gerber method for milk fat determination.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the advantages, limitations and precautions of the Gerber method for milk fat
  • determination /
  • Advantages; It is a rapid, simple and inexpensive method for determining fat content in milk.It is
  • widely used in dairy laboratories for routine milk quality analysis.
  • Limitations: The method uses concentrated sulphuric acid, which is corrosive and hazardous.
  • Incorrect acid concentration, temperature or centrifugation may lead to inaccurate results.
  • Precautions: Use the correct quantity and concentration of sulphuric acid and isoamyl alcohol.
  • Maintain the recommended temperature and centrifugation conditions, and read the fat column at
  • eye level.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the color development reaction in the Somogyi-Nelson method.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the colour development reaction in the Somogyi-Nelson method /
  • Reducing sugars reduce alkaline copper sulphate to cuprous oxide during heating.
  • Cuprous oxide reduces arsenomolybdate reagent to form a blue-coloured complex, whose
  • intensity is measured spectrophotometrically and is proportional to the reducing sugar
  • concentration.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the principle of Vitamin C estimation by the DCPIP method.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the principle of Vitamin C estimation by the DCPIP method /
  • Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) reduces the blue-coloured 2,6-dichlorophenolindophenol (DCPIP) dye
  • to its colourless reduced form.The amount of DCPIP decolourized is proportional to the vitamin
  • C content of the sample. The endpoint is indicated by a persistent light pink colour when a slight
  • excess of dye remains.

questions.question: Describe the construction, working principle, and applications of a hydrometer in food analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the construction, working principle and application of a hydrometer in food
  • analysis /
  • Construction: A hydrometer consists of a sealed glass tube with a weighted bulb at the bottom
  • and a graduated stem at the top.
  • Working principle:. It works on Archimedes’ principle: the hydrometer floats at a level
  • determined by the density or specific gravity of the liquid.
  • Applications: Measuring the specific gravity of milk, fruit juices, syrups and sugar solutions.
  • Estimating the concentration of dissolved substances in food liquids using suitable calibrated
  • hydrometers.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the different steps involved in the Kjeldahl method: digestion, distillation, and titration.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the different steps involved in the Kjeidahl method: digestion, distillation and
  • titration. /
  • Digestion: The sample is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid and a suitable catalyst,
  • converting organic nitrogen into ammonium sulphate.
  • Distillation: The digest is made alkaline with sodium hydroxide, releasing ammonia, which is
  • distilled and collected in boric acid or a suitable receiving solution.
  • Titration: The collected ammonia is titrated with a standard acid solution to determine the
  • nitrogen content.
  • Calculation: The nitrogen percentage is calculated and multiplied by an appropriate conversion
  • factor to estimate crude protein content.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: factor to estimate crude protein content.

questions.question: Differentiate between crude fiber and dietary fiber. Explain their importance in food analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between crude fibre and dietary fiber . Explain their importance in
  • food analysis /
  • Crude fibre is the residue remaining after acid and alkali digestion, whereas dietary fibre
  • includes non-digestible food components such as cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, pectin
  • and resistant starch.
  • Dietary fibre analysis provides a more accurate assessment of fibre content for nutritional
  • labelling and health evaluation, while crude fibre determination is mainly used in
  • conventional food composition analysis.

questions.question: Evaluate the importance of determining soluble, insoluble, and total dietary fiber in food and nutritional analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the importance of determining soluble, insoluble and total dietary fiber in
  • food and nutritional analysis /
  • Soluble fibre helps regulate blood glucose and cholesterol, while insoluble fibre increases
  • stool bulk and supports bowel regularity. Total dietary fibre provides an overall measure of
  • fibre content for nutritional labelling, quality control, dietary assessment and the
  • development of fibre-enriched foods.

questions.question: Write a detailed essay on the Modified Mojonnier method as a discontinuous solvent extraction technique for milk fat estimation. Include its principle, characteristics, step-by-step procedure, precautions, advantages, limitations, and applications in dairy and food analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a detailed essay on the Modified Mojonnier method as a discontinuous
  • solvent extraction technique for milk fat estimation. Include its principle,
  • characteristics, step by step procedure, precautions, advantages, limitations and
  • applications in dairy and food analysis. /
  • Principle and procedure: The Modified Mojonnier method is a discontinuous solvent
  • extraction technique. Ammonia helps release fat from the protein matrix, ethanol assists
  • extraction, and diethyl ether and petroleum ether extract the fat. The organic layers are
  • separated, combined, and evaporated; the remaining fat is dried and weighed to calculate
  • the fat percentage. Precautions, advantages, limitations and applications: Use clean, dry
  • glassware, ensure complete extraction and phase separation, avoid overheating, and handle
  • flammable solvents in a fume hood away from ignition sources. The method provides
  • reliable gravimetric fat estimation for dairy quality control and nutritional labelling, but it
  • is time-consuming, requires skilled handling and may produce errors from incomplete
  • extraction or solvent transfer losses.
